definitions.K2 surface key: casefold, whitespace-collapse, trailing 's / ’s stripped, leading honorific token(s) stripped repeatedly from the fixed list `honorifics`; the surname is surname_of() over the stripped original-case string, compared casefolded.
definitions.distinct_surface: K2 key distinct over the population; window = union of the windows of the volumes it appears in.
definitions.document_x_surface: (volume, document, K2 key) distinct — the person_mentions grain (one row per unique person per document).
definitions.novel_control: filtered-control detections whose span does not overlap (s < me and e > ms) any marked span in the same document; overlap computed here from spans, cross-checked against the raw control heads' `novel`.
definitions.surname_known (mention grain): m1a_survey.surname_of(text_of(surface)) is a key of by_surname (exact case; only officeholders with a dated appointment).
definitions.unique_by_document_year_among_dated: m1a's rule exactly: the document's TEI frus:doc-dateTime-min year, ±1.
definitions.unique_by_volume_window: exactly one POCOM officeholder with that surname has an appointment span overlapping [window_lo-1, window_hi+1], where the window is the manifest dateRange years of the VOLUME. PROXY: the store carries no document date. Bias: a multi-year window admits more officeholders than a document's own year, so this share is a LOWER bound on the per-document unique share m1a measured; the per-document figure is reported beside it wherever the TEI carries frus:doc-dateTime-min.
definitions.volume_x_surface: (volume, K2 key) distinct; window = the volume's.

novel_filtered_control_alone_mention_gra.caveat: 57.4% of the novel control's surname-known mentions (220,263 of 383,428) name nobody in office that year, and 47.0% (180,364) are single-token surfaces — given names (George, John) and places match POCOM surnames; the 32.9% is a string coincidence rate more than a candidate rate.

interpretation.eval_set: Planning/early-era-people/m1a-eval-candidates.csv: 300 rows, 0 keyed. It samples ONLY from/to names in the 12 m1a volumes, so once keyed it prices the MARKED from/to population (precision of 'the unique in-year officeholder is the person', and how often the person is in POCOM at all among the 'nobody in office' 17.2% and 'several' 8.0%); at 300 rows a ~55% rate carries a 95% half-width of about ±5.6 pts pooled and ±11 pts per 75-row band. It says NOTHING about the 1.18M novel-control surfaces, for which no ground truth exists; the M2a gold (64 of 72 documents, 406 mentions) is span-level and carries no identity column.
interpretation.marked_fromto_whole_scope: 235,218 from/to mentions with a surname over 267 volumes: 80.6% surname-known, 55.4% unique-by-document-year (m1a's 12-volume 83.2% / 63.9% overstated the unique ceiling by 8.5 pts; the sample's own store-based figure is 62.4%). Of the known, 40,563 (17.2% of with-surname) have NOBODY of that surname in office that year and 18,729 (8.0%) have several.
interpretation.primary_rule: unique_by_document_year (m1a's rule, TEI frus:doc-dateTime-min ±1) is PRIMARY: all 197,534 in-scope documents carry a TEI year, so the volume-window proxy was not needed; it is reported beside it and its bias is measured (it both loses and gains uniques: from/to whole scope loses 3,800 / gains 4,802, net +0.3 pt).

nearest_store_comparison_same_12_volumes.population: marked-layer rows with t in {from,to} over the 12 m1a volumes (ALL such rows, not only those in dated documents, and with no 8,000-char cut per document)

sample_population_gap_explained.explanation: the whole 653-row gap is m1a_survey.py's seg[:8000] cut per document segment; reading the full segment from the TEI gives 13,037 = the store's count exactly, and every from/to row sits in a dated document.
